TASK ID: vertex-cover-to-set-cover

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Vertex Cover to Set Cover. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Vertex Cover and TARGET is Set Cover. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = VertexCover
Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

TARGET = SetCover
Set Cover.

Instance: {"universe_size": u, "sets": [[element, ...], ...], "k": k}
  * The universe is the elements 0..u-1.
  * Each set lists distinct elements of the universe, in any order. A set
    may be empty, and the same set may appear more than once.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff AT MOST k of the sets together contain every element of the
universe.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. u = 0 is yes for every k >= 0 (choosing
no sets covers the empty universe). If some element is in no set, the
answer is no.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-c0lqfqd2

    reduce(instance) -> instance

The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

"""Polynomial-time reduction from Vertex Cover to Set Cover.

Vertex Cover instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
Set Cover instance:    {"universe_size": u, "sets": [[element, ...], ...], "k": k}

Reduction:
  * The universe is the set of edges; edge i is element i.
  * For every vertex v there is one set S_v containing the indices of all
    edges incident to v.
  * k is unchanged.

A collection of at most k sets covers every edge-element iff the
corresponding vertices form a vertex cover of size at most k.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    n = instance["n"]
    edges = instance["edges"]
    k = instance["k"]

    # Element i corresponds to edge i.
    universe_size = len(edges)
    sets = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    for i, (u, v) in enumerate(edges):
        sets[u].append(i)
        sets[v].append(i)

    return {"universe_size": universe_size, "sets": sets, "k": k}
EOF

import itertools
import random

import problems
from problems import VertexCover, SetCover
from reduce import reduce

tests_run = 0
tests_passed = 0


def check(instance):
    global tests_run, tests_passed
    tests_run += 1
    VertexCover.validate(instance)
    out = reduce(instance)
    SetCover.validate(out)
    expected = VertexCover.is_yes(instance)
    got = SetCover.is_yes(out)
    if expected == got:
        tests_passed += 1
    else:
        print("MISMATCH", instance, "->", out, "expected", expected, "got", got)
        raise AssertionError("reduction mismatch")


def all_graphs(n):
    pairs = [(u, v) for u in range(n) for v in range(u + 1, n)]
    for mask in range(1 << len(pairs)):
        edges = [list(p) for i, p in enumerate(pairs) if mask >> i & 1]
        yield edges


def main():
    # Exhaustive small graphs, all k values including negatives and large.
    for n in range(0, 5):
        for edges in all_graphs(n):
            for k in range(-2, n + 3):
                check({"n": n, "edges": edges, "k": k})

    # Random larger instances.
    rng = random.Random(12345)
    for _ in range(3000):
        n = rng.randint(0, 8)
        pairs = [(u, v) for u in range(n) for v in range(u + 1, n)]
        edges = [list(p) for p in pairs if rng.random() < 0.4]
        k = rng.randint(-1, n + 1)
        check({"n": n, "edges": edges, "k": k})

    # Use the provided random_instance generators too.
    for scale in range(0, 7):
        for _ in range(200):
            inst = VertexCover.random_instance(rng, scale)
            check(inst)

    print(f"tests_run={tests_run} tests_passed={tests_passed}")
    assert tests_run == tests_passed


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
EOF

A collection of at most k sets covers every edge-element iff the
corresponding vertices form a vertex cover of size at most k.

    edges = instance["edges"]
    k = instance["k"]

    universe_size = len(edges)
    sets = [[] for _ in range(n)]
